title: Autonomous Lean-Verified Proof of Erdős Problem #728 (GPT-5.2 Pro & Aristotle)
whyItMatters: Watershed moment of early 2026: GPT-5.2 Pro and Harmonic’s Aristotle autonomously produced a Lean-checked proof of a 30-year-open Erdős problem, confirmed by Terence Tao.
summary: In January 2026, GPT-5.2 Pro generated a novel proof of Paul Erdős’s open factorial-divisibility Problem #728, which Harmonic’s Aristotle agent formalized and machine-checked in Lean 4. Terence Tao publicly confirmed the solution as an early milestone where an AI pipeline resolved a genuinely open Erdős problem largely autonomously, kicking off the 2026 wave of AI-solved Erdős problems.
technicalHighlights: Combined frontier natural-language reasoning (GPT-5.2 Pro) with automated Lean 4 formalization (Harmonic Aristotle).
Confirmed by Terence Tao and logged on the official teorth/erdosproblems AI contributions wiki.
Catalyzed rapid community adoption of LLM-to-Lean workflows for attacking long-tail open conjectures.
caveats: Problem #728 was a relatively accessible open Erdős problem rather than a central structural conjecture, and minor edge-case tightening was refined during community review.

scoreRationale.foundational: Modest individual theorem depth, but a historic proof-of-concept for autonomous resolution of open problems.
scoreRationale.ripple: Triggered an explosion of independent researchers deploying LLM + Lean loops on open conjecture lists.
scoreRationale.verification: Lean 4 formally verified and explicitly confirmed by Terence Tao.
scoreRationale.velocity: Marked the inflection point where open Erdős problems began falling in hours rather than decades.
